title: Relative shifts up to 2 ms permit model source ambiguity at 5 percent error in 29 of 133 selected Allen input pairs
abstract: We tested whether fitted voltage waveforms can identify which of two connected source cells was active. We used 133 pairs of excitatory inputs to shared targets in Allen cortical slice data: 89 mouse VisP pairs and 44 human TCx pairs. With exact fitted kernels and free positive amplitudes, the least relative L2 waveform error that permits a common response is sqrt((1-rho)/2), where rho is the normalized waveform overlap. At a 5 percent error bound, 5 mouse pairs and 1 human pair permit source ambiguity with known spike time. A grid of relative shifts from -2 to +2 ms gives ambiguity witnesses in 20 mouse pairs and 9 human pairs. The grid counts are lower bounds for continuous timing freedom. An independent high precision calculation agrees within 1.3e-11 in the error threshold. These are deterministic model results, not measured decoding errors. Uncertain fits, separate recordings, selected slice circuits and assumed event timing limit biological inference. Original code, aggregate results, a figure, source hashes and an external data recipe support reproduction. External source records are excluded from the bundle.

display.caption: Fraction of selected input pairs with a common possible waveform at each relative L2 error bound. The timing grid gives explicit witnesses, not a continuous global optimum. Pair weights are equal; these curves are descriptive model results.
